subject: Onboarding: NovaHealth private VPC — visibility & SIEM handoff
messages:
From: Samira Patel <samira@novahealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding: NovaHealth private VPC — visibility & SIEM handoff

Hi Marissa / Kim,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We've pulled together the initial evidence checklist and a short set of questions for the private deployment (VPC) visibility handoff. Our security team needs clarity on the following so we can sign off on inbound routing to our Splunk Cloud HEC endpoint: 

- Single-tenant HEC? We plan to provide a dedicated HEC token and dedicated ingest endpoint in our account. Need confirmation on mutual TLS support and certs.
- Network ports and egress model: whether Redwood will push (agent/forwarder) out to our HEC or if we must open an inbound path to an internal forwarder.
- Trace propagation: can Redwood emit W3C traceparent on upstream requests and include trace hooks in exported spans?
- Sample payloads: we need sample syslog and span payloads for our SIEM mapping and schema validation.

I've attached the evidence spreadsheet (novahealth-evidence-req.xlsx) that lists items they expect for SOC review. Can you confirm what's reasonable to provide from the private control plane vs. what we'll need to collect from our side?

Thanks,
Samira
Security Operations
NovaHealth

Attachment: novahealth-evidence-req.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Samira Patel <samira@novahealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding: NovaHealth private VPC — visibility & SIEM handoff

Samira — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then proposed next steps below.

Quick answers:
- Mutual TLS: supported. For Private (VPC) deployments we can present a client cert from the forwarder -> your HEC. We will coordinate a CSR exchange (or accept your CA).
- Ingest model: Redwood's recommended pattern for regulated workloads is a customer-hosted HEC with a Redwood forwarder inside your VPC (forwarder pulls logs from local runtime sockets and pushes to the HEC). We can also support a push from a Redwood-managed forwarder over a restricted egress path if you prefer (requires explicit firewall rules).
- Trace propagation: yes — the runtime can emit W3C traceparent/span ids and include them in exported traces. We add a tracehook that annotates generation requests with a redwood.request_id header; we'll include mapping docs.
- Sample payloads: attached are two artifacts: the onramp runbook (redwood-private-siem-onramp.md) and a small network-port-mapping CSV we use internally. These should help your SIEM mappings.

Proposed next steps:
1) Security sync (30m) where we review the novahealth-evidence-req.xlsx and mark items: "Redwood-provided" vs "Customer-provided".
2) Cert exchange: we'll generate a CSR and share. Kimberly will own the cert flow.
3) On-prem forwarder deployment: provide a small docker-compose and systemd example to run the forwarder inside the VPC. We'll schedule a handoff with your infra team for a test ingest.

I'll loop in Jonas for the HEC mapping and port specifics. If that works, propose Tue 6/25 10am PT.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-private-siem-onramp.md (6KB), network-port-mapping.csv (1KB)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding: NovaHealth private VPC — visibility & SIEM handoff

Marissa / Jonas — digging into the details from the runbook, a few implementation notes we should confirm with NovaHealth before the cert exchange: 

- TLS handshake: NovaHealth should confirm whether they enforce client cert CN constraints. If so we need the CN pattern to set in the CSR.
- HEC auth/batching: Splunk HEC can accept gzip'd JSON batches. We'll offer a batching config (max_batch_size=5MB, max_interval=2s) to avoid token throttling.
- Network ports: the forwarder needs outbound 443 to HEC host; if they want us to open inbound we'll need a NATed IP range for the forwarder. See attached CSV for the port map we typically use.
- Trace hooks: For compatibility with their APM, we'll add an optional span attribute redwood.model.name and redwood.model.variant; Jonas, please confirm naming conventions and whether we need to include sampling priority.

Operational checklist for the test handoff (short):
- Provide HEC test endpoint + token (test, not prod).
- Confirm whether HEC is fronted by load balancer that strips client certs.
- Provide a small firewall rule for our test forwarder IP if they require source-based allow list.

I'll prepare the CSR template and a docker-compose example before Tue.

Kimberly
Director, Platform Security — Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com

Date: Sat, 22 Jun 2028 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding: NovaHealth private VPC — visibility & SIEM handoff

Samira — thanks, this looks good. A couple of concrete deliverables from Redwood that we'll include in the test bundle: 

- Sample payloads: 3 sample events (syslog JSON, HEC batch JSON, and an OTLP span export) with example mappings to Splunk fields. I'll drop them in the Drive link and send back a HubSpot note with the file ids.
- Runbook steps: exact docker-compose snippet to run the forwarder (binds to /var/log/redwood-runtime; exposes a local HTTP health endpoint on 127.0.0.1:9411 for trace verification).
- Trace mapping: we'll include a short doc describing redwood.request_id -> splunk_transaction_id mapping and optional redwood.model.* tags.

Planned timeline: cert exchange & CSR on Mon 6/24; test ingest Tue 6/25; SIEM mapping sign-off Wed 6/26. If they want an alternate cadence we can adjust.

Action items for NovaHealth to send before the cert exchange:
- HEC test endpoint and a test token (we'll use token scope restricted to test index).
- Any CA that will be used to sign client certs (or permission to use our client cert signed by Redwood test CA).
- Confirmation of any mid-path LB that might terminate TLS.

I'll upload the samples to the linked Drive folder and post the HubSpot ticket id once created.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Visibility & Integrations Lead — Redwood Inference
